key_insight: SILSA replaces fragmented voxel-based 3D generation with compact sliding-window slice latents, helping preserve surface continuity and topology in high-resolution shapes. The key idea is to generate 3D structure more coherently while reducing token count and generation cost.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the inefficiency and topology errors of existing high-resolution 3D generation pipelines, which often split shapes into many local tokens and struggle with thin structures or highly connected geometries.
method: Represents 3D objects using compact slice latents computed over sliding windows rather than dense voxel tokens.
Uses a topology-aware generation strategy to maintain continuous surfaces across neighboring slices.
Supports high-resolution 3D synthesis with fewer tokens, reducing fragmentation and improving structural consistency.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SILSA offers a more efficient way to generate detailed 3D shapes while better preserving topology. This can improve quality in applications like 3D modeling, robotics, CAD, and generative design where continuity and geometric fidelity matter.

paper_title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
paper_authors: Tianjiao Yu, Xinzhuo Li, Yifan Shen, Ying Shen, Kiet A. Nguyen
